labels.text: List catalog models and discovered local models.
No models available to this CLI account tier.

S105.04.needs: an account or API key that can call models
S105.04.note: The text output shows context and output sizes; the capability flags appear only in the --json output.
steps: Open a terminal and sign in to the CLI with an account or key that can call models (agi login).
Type agi models list and press Return.
Read each model line: it shows the context window and the max output size.
Type agi models list --json and look for supports_tools, supports_vision and supports_reasoning on each model.
Compare with Expected: the models your key can call, with capabilities and context size.
S105.04.where: Terminal > agi models list (add --json for the JSON form)

S105.12.note: No in-app command to save a prompt template was found; saved prompts are markdown files under ~/.agiworkforce/prompts/claude (apps/cli/src/custom_commands.rs:6) offered as /prompts:<name> (apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs:33), and the loader that feeds them to the registry and any argument substitution for them were not found, so searched apps/cli for save, prompt template, and prompts.

labels.text: Show the account's managed allowance from the shared usage ledger.
Show session credit usage by model

S105.18.note: Usage shows credits rather than dollars, and the history is unavailable outside a managed account.
steps: Sign in with a managed account (not a local-only or BYOK setup).
Type agi usage and press Return.
Read the line that starts Usage history, and the By model: list under it.
Look at the Week of or month lines under the history to see usage over time.
Compare with Expected: usage and cost over time, broken down by model.
S105.18.where: Terminal > agi usage (in the chat, /cost shows session credit usage by model)

labels.text: No spend cap for this session. /budget <credits> sets one per turn.

S105.20.note: The code shows no owner-set cap enforced by the API; --max-budget-usd only emits a budget_exhausted status event (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:491 and 9283).
steps: Start the CLI with agi and open a chat.
Type /budget 500 and press Return, then read the reply about stopping each turn after 500 credits.
Type /budget alone and check that it shows the cap.
Type /budget off and check that the reply says the spend cap was removed.
Compare with Expected: an owner sets a spend cap that the API enforces. The /budget cap is set by the user per turn in the CLI.
S105.20.where: Chat > type /budget <credits> (for example /budget 500), or agi --max-budget-usd <USD> on the top-level command

The closest is agi doctor --export, whose help text says 'Write a redacted diagnostics file to review and attach to a support request.' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1044), which is a file, not a channel.

S105.29.note: Whether a plain local folder is accepted as the install source is not confirmed (apps/cli/src/installs.rs:93 handles git sources; the local-path branch was not read), and the agi plugin digest command comes from a doc comment, not a read of its subcommand entry.
steps: Pick an unpublished plugin folder on disk.
Type agi plugin digest <folder> and copy the sha256:<hex> value it prints.
Type agi plugin install <folder> --integrity sha256:<hex> and press Return.
Type agi plugin list and look for the plugin name in the installed list.
Compare with Expected: the unpublished plugin loads into your own account so you can try it.
S105.29.where: Terminal > agi plugin install <folder> --integrity sha256:<hex> (get the hash from agi plugin digest <folder>)
